clue.text: Marked by experience, demon goes back home

indicators.note: goes back tells us the word for a demon is read from right to left

parts.note: a demon is a devil
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A fiend retreats to its lair, battle-scarred after its adventures.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'demon' as the subject of 'goes back home', but 'goes back' only reverses the demon's word; 'home' supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lived-in shows signs of long use, so it bears the marks of experience.

clue.text: In battle, a dragoon is shot

indicators.note: In tells us the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cavalry soldier is wounded in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to the letters within battLE A Dragoon; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is the metal used for bullets, so shot is lead in the collective sense.

clue.text: Peter out, without right coat

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for peter out goes round the letter for right

parts.note: to peter out is to fade away or vanish

explanation.surface: Someone runs short of paint and fails to apply the correct coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so VANISH encloses R. It looks like 'lacking', the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is a coat of clear protective finish applied to wood.

clue.text: Lived and died on the border

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees
a welt is a strip or border, especially on a shoe or garment

explanation.surface: Someone spent their life and ended it on the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: A welt is the edging strip on a shoe, so 'border' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, meaning resided or lived.

clue.text: Peer picking up good French lover

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means the French word for good is read upwards

parts.note: bon is French for good
leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A member of the House of Lords takes up with a French paramour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' turns BON to NOB in this down clue. LEMAN is an old poetic word for a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: Address in Ontario misspelt

indicators.note: misspelt says the letters of the province's name are written in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A speech delivered in Canada has the province's name spelt wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misspelt' rearranges the letters of ONTARIO; 'in' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech is an address, the same sense as in a public address.

clue.text: State predetermined no borders

indicators.note: no borders says the word for predetermined loses its first and last letters

parts.note: foregone means predetermined, as in a foregone conclusion

explanation.surface: A frontier-free US state is a done deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no borders' strips the first and last letters from FOREGONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the states of the USA on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: A way to call up, showing no emotion

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for call is read upwards

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as before a court

explanation.surface: Someone telephones in a flat, unmoved manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CITE into ETIC in this down clue; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means indifferent, lacking feeling or interest.

clue.text: Throw in some writing material — blue, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: ink is some writing material and blue means lewd, as in a blue film; said together they make the sound heard

explanation.surface: Someone tosses in some sapphire-coloured ink.
explanation.walkthrough: INK plus LEWD spoken together gives the answer. 'blue' means risqué here, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw in something extra is to include it, as in a sales deal.

clue.text: He torments shifty characters at the bottom of the pile

definitions.text: at the bottom of the pile

indicators.note: shifty characters means the letters move about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bully tortures dodgy people at the foot of the heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifty characters' rearranges HETORMENTS; 'characters' means letters, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest of all, so the item furthest down in a heap.

clue.text: A stretch of grass that's been cut by competent and pleasant …

indicators.note: that's been cut says the word for a stretch of grass has lost its final letter

parts.note: a green is a stretch of grass, as on a village green
competent means able

explanation.surface: Someone praises a lawn that has just been mown and is neat and nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been cut' takes the last letter off GREEN, leaving GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable and pleasant are synonyms for something nice to experience.

clue.text: … Caledonian attending a sporting venue

indicators.note: attending is used in the sense of following on, so one piece comes after the other

parts.note: Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scotsman goes along to a sports ground, continuing the previous clue's sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the racecourse in Berkshire famous for Royal Ascot. 'attending' places SCOT after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, a sporting venue given by example.

clue.text: In disgrace, thrashed one's hide? Tough

indicators.note: thrashed suggests the letters are beaten about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who has done wrong gets a beating — hard luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrashed' rearranges ONESHIDETOUGH; it looks like part of the punishment picture, which is the disgrace of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doghouse is an idiom for being out of favour after some misdeed.

clue.text: Root out heart of problem, and then do it again

indicators.note: heart of takes the three central letters of the word problem

parts.note: to iterate is to repeat or do again

explanation.surface: Advice to eradicate the core of an issue, then repeat the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes OBL, the middle three letters of prOBLem; 'and then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To root out is to destroy completely, which is to obliterate.

clue.text: Unconventional half of book Tarzan, say — I was in

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of the word book
this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: Tarzan is an example of a he-man, a muscular macho type

explanation.surface: Someone recalls their wild youth reading half a Tarzan novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was in' is the container signal; some solvers felt its past tense makes a weak instruction. A he-man is a muscular hero type.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian lives outside social norms, so the word describes an unconventional person.

clue.text: Decorative woodwork — make sample

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand, especially of car
to try is to sample or taste

explanation.surface: A craftsman makes a trial piece of ornamental joinery.
explanation.walkthrough: MARQUE is a make in the brand sense, as with classic cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is inlaid veneer forming patterns, a form of decorative woodwork.

clue.text: Run into one form of water or another

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for run goes inside the word for one form of water

parts.note: steam is water in vapour form
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A remark about water changing from one state to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside STEAM. The definition reads on from the wordplay: a stream is another form of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a further kind of water, completing the phrase about one form or another.

clue.text: Doctor urges pub to disclose dangerous sort of bacterium

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician tells a bar to reveal a nasty germ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb rearranging URGESPUB; 'to disclose' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A superbug is a bacterium resistant to antibiotics and so dangerous.

clue.text: Batting, decided to take on cover

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
decided means sure, as in 'definite'

explanation.surface: A batsman makes up their mind to buy protection.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'in' while the other side fields.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure is to arrange a policy giving financial protection, or cover.

clue.text: Help susceptible person to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the word for a susceptible person is spoken

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible or easily taken-in person

explanation.surface: Aid is sought for someone vulnerable who wants a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: SUCKER and the answer sound alike in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is assistance given in time of need, so help.

clue.text: Look aggressive at first, losing time

parts.note: butch means tough and aggressively masculine

indicators.note: losing says a letter is taken away from the word for at first

parts.note: erst is an archaic word meaning at first or formerly

explanation.surface: Someone advises you to look fierce initially, then ease off as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops T from ERST, leaving ERS. BUTCHERS is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Butcher's, short for butcher's hook, is Cockney rhyming slang for a look.

clue.text: Wind bearing round spit

indicators.note: round says the bearing goes around the word for spit

parts.note: ENE, east-north-east, is a compass bearing
spit, as in 'the spit of', means an exact double or twin

explanation.surface: A breeze blows from some direction around a roasting spit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spit' means an exact lookalike, as in 'the dead spit of', not a roasting skewer; 'Wind' is the verb, not the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or wind things together.

clue.text: Stifle two mothers

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal such as a horse
a pen is a female swan, so a mother swan

explanation.surface: Two mothers try to suppress something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two mothers' yields two pieces: DAM, an animal's mother, and PEN, a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen is to deaden or muffle, so to stifle enthusiasm or sound.

clue.text: Bravery people in hospital department show shot in the arm

indicators.note: in places the words for bravery and people inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
bravery means courage
men means people

explanation.surface: Patients in a hospital ward put on a show of bravery while having injections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot in the arm is an idiom for a boost or stimulus that heartens someone.

clue.text: Lamb's enjoyable, looking increasingly appetising now they've started

indicators.note: now they've started points to the opening letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Roast lamb looks more and more tempting as it cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote essays under the name Elia, so ELIAN means of Lamb. The first letters of 'enjoyable, looking, increasingly, appetising, now' give it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elian means relating to Charles Lamb, whose pen name was Elia.

clue.text: Band in port

definitions.meaning: a rubber band fitted round a wheel
an ancient port city of Lebanon

explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is the band round a wheel, and Tyre is a Lebanese port.

clue.text: A room that's up high

parts.note: a loft is a room in the roof space

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes an attic.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft is an adverb meaning overhead, raised above the ground.

clue.text: Marketing house allowed you to make a start

parts.note: a public house is a pub
licit means lawful or allowed

indicators.note: to make a start signals taking only the opening letter of the word you

explanation.surface: An estate agency gives you permission to begin work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a start' takes the first letter Y from 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity is promotion of a product or person, a near synonym of marketing.

clue.text: 4 that is before long …

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, a peer, and an earl is one
yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in 'yon hill'

explanation.surface: A cross-reference followed by an explanatory 'that is' leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word. 4 down is NOBLEMAN, of which an earl is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Early on means at an early stage, which is soon or before long.

clue.text: … working on geese from Italy

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Birds from an Italian city are put to work, continuing the previous clue's sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ONGEESE. GENOESE means from Genoa in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoese describes something from Genoa, so it is an Italian place adjective.
